name: Dialog
purpose: A modal window for one short, focused task, such as naming a new project, that a person finishes or cancels before returning to the page.
description: A focused modal for a single task. Native dialog manages focus containment and Escape. The form validates before confirming.

guidance.summary: A modal window for one short, focused task, such as naming a new project, that a person finishes or cancels before returning to the page.
useWhen: A short task needs the person’s full attention and only a few fields.
The page behind should stay exactly where it was while the task is done.

avoidWhen.text: Confirming an action that deletes, sends, or pays.
The task is long, or people need to look at the page while doing it.
Showing a few options next to the control that opened them.
A warning or information people can read where they are.

states.label: Closed
states.description: Only the button that opens it is visible.

states.label: Open
states.description: The dialog sits over a dimmed page. Focus moves into it and stays there.
states.how: Press the trigger; the dialog opens with showModal().

states.label: Invalid
states.description: Submitting a missing or wrong value keeps the dialog open and names the problem at the field.
states.how: Submit with a required field empty.

states.label: Dismissed
states.description: Escape, Cancel, or the close button closes it without saving, and focus returns to the trigger.
states.how: Escape, Cancel, or the close button.

dos.text: Title the dialog with the task, and repeat its verb on the primary button: Create a project, then Create project.
dos.why: People confirm the thing they started, not a generic OK.

dos.text: Keep it to one task and a few fields.
dos.why: A dialog covers the page; the longer it gets, the more people lose their place.

dos.text: Always offer a way out: Cancel, the close button, and Escape.
dos.why: A window people cannot leave feels like a trap.

dos.text: Return focus to the button that opened it when it closes.
dos.why: Keyboard and screen reader users carry on from where they were.

donts.text: Don’t open a dialog that nobody asked for.
donts.why: Unrequested windows interrupt work and get dismissed unread.

donts.text: Don’t open a dialog on top of another dialog.
donts.why: With two layers, it is unclear what Cancel will close.

donts.text: Don’t close it on a click outside while it holds what someone typed.
donts.why: One stray click should not throw away their work.

donts.text: Don’t put a page’s main content or navigation in a dialog.
donts.why: Content inside a dialog cannot be linked to, bookmarked, or found again.

content: Title: the task in sentence case, such as Create a project.
Primary button: the same verb and its object, such as Create project. The other button is Cancel.
Add one short sentence under the title only when the task needs context.

keyboard.action: Move between the controls inside the dialog.

notes: A native dialog element opened with showModal(): the page behind becomes inert and focus stays inside.
aria-labelledby points to the title, so the dialog is announced by its name.
The close button has its own accessible name, Close dialog.
